title: US Records Net TIC Inflow in August
body: The United States registered a net Treasury International Capital (TIC) inflow of $199.8 billion in August 2026, driven by foreign purchases of both long-term and short-term US securities, as well as cross-border banking flows. Net foreign private inflows amounted to $178.5 billion, while net foreign official inflows totaled $21.3 billion. Foreign residents recorded net purchases of $300.7 billion in long-term US securities, including $257.8 billion from private investors and $42.9 billion from official institutions. By contrast, foreign residents cut their holdings of US Treasury bills by $47.8 billion. Combined holdings of other dollar-denominated short-term US securities and custody liabilities declined by $37.8 billion, and US banks' net dollar-denominated liabilities to foreign residents decreased by $41.6 billion. title: Ibovespa Advances on IBC-Br Rebound
body: The Ibovespa advanced 0.5% on Friday, closing at 205,430, supported by fresh economic activity data and a pause in the recent oil rally. The Central Bank of Brazil's Economic Activity Index (IBC-Br) rose 0.3% month-over-month in August, matching market expectations and reversing a 0.2% contraction in July. The improvement was driven by sectors oriented toward the domestic market, especially those tied to household income, which benefited from slower price increases in essential items such as food. Utilities finished mostly higher, with Axia up 0.6% and Sabesp gaining 1%. Retailers and non-durable goods producers also moved higher, including a 0.9% rise in Ambev and a 4.2% jump in Assaí. Meanwhile, Petrobras climbed 4% as oil prices stayed elevated amid growing supply risks stemming from escalating tensions in the Middle East and in the Russia–Ukraine conflict. Despite Friday's gains, the Ibovespa ended the week down 0.5%. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: TSX Edges Higher as Energy Gains Offset Tech Selloff
body: The S&P/TSX Composite Index inched up 0.1% to close at 36,177 on Friday, paring earlier gains as a broad selloff in North American technology stocks deepened. Shopify slid 5.1%, pressured by an eighth straight session of losses in U.S. chipmakers—the sector's longest losing streak since the 2008 financial crisis. Shopify's partnership with Meta has further heightened its exposure to the AI trade. Celestica declined 3.9%, while Constellation Software lost 3%. By contrast, energy producers buoyed the index as crude prices climbed on growing supply concerns. Canadian Natural Resources advanced 3.2%, Suncor and Cenovus each rose 2.7%, and Imperial Oil gained 2.9%. Energy infrastructure names also helped offset tech-sector weakness, with Enbridge up 2.3%. Bank stocks were muted after hawkish comments from the Bank of Canada's governor, while miners ended mixed as gold and silver prices retreated. For the week, the S&P/TSX Composite Index was up 0.8%. title: US Budget Swings to Deficit in September
body: The US government posted a $27 billion budget deficit in September 2026, reversing a $198 billion surplus in the same month a year earlier, but slightly outperforming market expectations for a $29 billion deficit. Federal outlays rose sharply to $585 billion from $346 billion the year before. The largest spending categories were Social Security ($141 billion), health programs ($100 billion), Medicare ($93 billion), and national defense ($89 billion). Government receipts also increased, climbing to $558 billion from $544 billion. The main revenue sources were individual income taxes ($298 billion), social insurance and retirement contributions ($149 billion), and corporate income taxes ($87 billion). For the full 2026 fiscal year, the cumulative federal budget deficit reached $1.992 trillion. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com
